votes.reasoning: The defect is fixed. AtomicFileWrite.swift:42-44 creates the temp file with the requested mode and swaps it in with rename(2), so an older 0644 destination ends at 0600. The symlink guard runs before the temp file exists (AtomicFileWrite.swift:37-40). It uses lstat on the last path component and throws AppError.io; Paths.ensureDir already refuses a symlinked directory. There is a small gap between the lstat and the rename, but rename replaces the link itself and never follows it, so a link planted in that gap cannot redirect the secret. I ran --filter "AtomicFileWrite|ConfigLoader|FileCredentialReader|CreditBaseline": 98 tests in 12 suites passed. Reversal A: I disabled only the symlink guard (changed :38 to `if false, ...`). symlinked_destination_is_refused then failed at AtomicFileWriteTests.swift:97 (no error was thrown) and :102 (the link was replaced by a regular file). Reversal B: I restored the HEAD body, adding only the test-seam call. existing_loose_destination_is_tightened failed at :34 (mode was not 0600), which matches the Ferreiro's RED line. Under HEAD the symlink test also passed, so the old replaceItemAt path refused symlinks too. The guard therefore keeps existing behaviour; without it, round 1's bare rename would have silently replaced the link. I restored the fixed file afterwards, and git diff is byte-identical to reviews/diffs/B6-files-tests-r2.diff. Production callers: DiskCache:148/165, PinStore:65, UsageHistoryStore:192, CreditBaseline:239 and OpenAIResetJournal:30 all write files the app creates itself inside Paths directories, and ensureDir refuses those directories when they are symlinks, so none of these is legitimately a symlink. ConfigLoader:110/189/276 (config.toml) and FileCredentialReader:74 (~/.codex/auth.json, only with the opt-in refresh) can be user symlinks. For those, the write now fails loudly and nothing on disk changes, which is the documented decision (doc comment at :18-22, README:531). Caveat: AppEnvironment.swift:23 calls ensureAllVendorSections through try?, so on a symlinked config.toml that append is skipped without any message. That is pre-existing, since HEAD refused too.

Round 2 adds a symlink refusal at Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cache/AtomicFileWrite.swift:37-40. It is one guard at nesting depth 1, and it runs before the temp file is created, so the refusal path needs no cleanup. The function body went from about 14 lines to 17. The old existingMode(of:) helper became lstatMode(of:) at :55-59 instead of a second stat call being added next to it, so there is still one call and no duplication. The new name is accurate: it returns the full st_mode from lstat, and the doc comment says so. The permission bits are masked once, at the single use (:43). The refusal throws AppError.io, the error type the rest of the function already uses. Nothing is swallowed, and the one try? is still the temp-file cleanup at :48, which the repo allows as best-effort. The doc comment at :18-25 explains why a symlink is refused (rename would replace the link, and writing through it could redirect a secret) instead of restating the code. The README security section gets a matching line, which follows the docs-in-lockstep rule. The new test Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/AtomicFileWriteTests.swift symlinked_destination_is_refused has an accurate name and checks one fact per assertion: it throws, the link is still a link, the target's contents and mode are unchanged, and no temp file is left. It compares the Optional FileAttributeType through expectTrue, as CLAUDE.md section 3 requires. It adds no new abstraction and no logging.

Both round-1 required changes are done. (1) The symlinked-destination behaviour is now a deliberate, pinned decision. AtomicFileWrite.swift checks the destination with lstatMode and throws AppError.io on S_IFLNK before any temp file is created. Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/AtomicFileWriteTests.swift:89-107 (symlinked_destination_is_refused) asserts four things: the call throws, the link is still a symlink, the target's content and 0644 mode are unchanged, and no temp file is left behind. (2) The behaviour is documented in the AtomicFileWrite doc comment (symlink refusal, plus the xattr/ACL loss caused by the inode swap) and in README.md:531 next to the existing 'TOCTOU symlink refusal' line. The public signature write(_:to:permissions:) is unchanged, and the tempWritten seam is internal. Every file in `git diff --stat` ties to a batch id. For this id the relevant files are AtomicFileWrite.swift, AtomicFileWriteTests.swift, Validate/main.swift and README.md. The other files belong to the other B6 ids (DiskCache now/TEST-ARG-012, the provider E2E tests, and so on). Refusing a symlinked config.toml or auth.json changes behaviour, but the launch path is not bricked: AppEnvironment.swift:23 calls ensureAllVendorSections through try?. See new_findings.
